User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want to enter a vendor’s base rate, so that all pricing calculations start from accurate cost data.
Description: Vendor cost is the foundation of the entire pricing and margin engine. The system must require vendor base rate entry before allowing any quote to be finalized. Vendor cost changes must be traceable and must not retroactively impact approved or posted invoices.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Vendor base rate required before finalization.
2. Accept two-decimal currency only.
3. Reject zero or negative values.
4. Log old value, new value, user, timestamp.
5. Preserve historical cost snapshot on posted invoices.
Notes: Core calculation dependency. Snapshot logic mandatory.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want the system to apply a 35 percent target margin automatically, so that pricing aligns with company standards.
Description: 35 percent is the expected margin per sale. Suggested pricing must be calculated consistently using centralized formula logic.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Suggested rate = Vendor Cost / (1 - 0.35).
2. Default margin configurable by Administrator (Admin).
3. Recalculate instantly when vendor cost changes.
4. Show suggested and actual rate side-by-side.
5. Round to two decimals consistently.
Notes: Avoid duplicated formula logic between frontend and backend.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want margin updated in real time, so that I understand profitability impact before saving.
Description: Users must see profitability impact immediately during pricing adjustments.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Update margin instantly on price or cost change.
2. Include all cost components.
3. Green indicator if >= target.
4. Red warning if below threshold.
5. Tooltip shows formula breakdown.
Notes: Prevents blind pricing during live calls.

Task Name: Compare Preferred Service Provider (PSP) to Statistical Rate
User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want to compare Preferred Service Provider (PSP) pricing to statistical rates, so that I can choose the most profitable option.
Description: Statistical pricing provides benchmark comparison to optimize sourcing decisions.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Display PSP and statistical rate side-by-side.
2. Calculate margin for both options.
3. Allow user to select final option.
4. Log selected pricing source.
5. Show warning if statistical data unavailable.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want margin recalculated if vendor cost changes before approval, so that profitability remains accurate.
Description: Vendor changes must not silently reduce margin.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Recalculate margin automatically after vendor edit.
2. Trigger approval if below threshold.
3. Notify assigned Account Manager (AM).
4. Preserve original snapshot once approved.
5. Do not modify posted invoices.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want low-margin quotes to require approval, so that pricing governance is enforced.
Description: Quotes below threshold must not finalize without oversight.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Enter Pending Approval state.
2. Block finalization until approved.
3. Notify Customer Success Manager (CSM).
4. Log approval decision.
5. Return to draft if rejected.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want extremely low margins escalated to higher management, so that high-risk pricing receives executive oversight.
Description: Severe margin deviations require multi-level approval.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Configurable multi-tier thresholds.
2. Auto-route based on margin level.
3. Lock quote until final decision.
4. Display approval chain.
5. Log all approval steps.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want totals calculated based on quantity, so that revenue and margin reflect actual units sold.
Description: Quantity must multiply vendor and customer rates correctly.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Vendor total = rate x quantity.
2. Customer total = rate x quantity.
3. Margin calculated on aggregate totals.
4. Prevent quantity zero.
5. Recalculate instantly on change.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want delivery and removal fees separated, so that margin clarity is preserved per component.
Description: Blended fees obscure profitability reporting.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Display delivery and removal as separate line items.
2. Calculate margin per line.
3. Require approval if waived below threshold.
4. Preserve breakdown on invoice.
5. Support reporting by fee type.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want margin snapshot stored at approval time, so that reports reflect original decision context.
Description: Margin must not recalculate historically.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Store margin, cost, and price at approval.
2. Lock snapshot after posting.
3. Reports reference stored snapshot.
4. Log approver and timestamp.
5. Prevent overwrite from later edits.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want manual overrides logged, so that pricing deviations are traceable.
Description: Overrides must never be silent.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Require justification text.
2. Log original and overridden margin.
3. Store user and timestamp.
4. Flag override in reports.
5. Prevent deletion of override history.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want mandatory justification when margin is below threshold, so that accountability is enforced.
Description: Low-margin decisions must include explanation.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Require minimum character count.
2. Block finalization without justification.
3. Store justification in approval record.
4. Visible in reports.
5. Log submission time.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want settlement adjustments reflected in margin reporting, so that final profitability is accurate.
Description: Post-service settlements must update margin visibility.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Calculate final margin after settlement.
2. Preserve original quoted margin.
3. Display variance between quoted and final.
4. Log settlement adjustment.
5. Include in exports.

User Story: As a Director, I want margin variance tracked, so that profitability drift is visible.
Description: Variance tracking supports executive visibility.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Calculate approved vs final margin delta.
2. Highlight deviations beyond threshold.
3. Filter by date and region.
4. Drill-down to quote level.
5. Exportable report.

User Story: As an Administrator (Admin), I want configurable approval thresholds, so that governance rules can adapt over time.
Description: Margin thresholds must not be hard-coded.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Admin panel to edit threshold.
2. Log changes.
3. Apply to new quotes only.
4. Validate 0–100 percent range.
5. Support multi-tier configuration.

User Story: As an Administrator (Admin), I want margin edits restricted by role, so that unauthorized users cannot alter profitability.
Description: Not all roles should modify pricing.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Restrict editing to CSS and CSM.
2. Viewer roles read-only.
3. Log attempted unauthorized edits.
4. Display read-only indicator.
5. Permission matrix configurable.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want a hard minimum margin enforced, so that extremely unprofitable deals cannot proceed.
Description: Some margins should be impossible to approve.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Define hard minimum percent.
2. Block quote below minimum.
3. Display blocking message.
4. Log attempt.
5. Allow override only by Admin.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want a dashboard queue of pending approvals, so that low-margin requests are processed quickly.
Description: Visibility prevents approval bottlenecks.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Show count of pending approvals.
2. Filter by region or user.
3. Sort by margin severity.
4. Link directly to quote.
5. Update in real time.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want pricing source decisions tracked, so that sourcing performance is measurable.
Description: Selection tracking informs vendor strategy.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Store selected pricing source.
2. Log user and timestamp.
3. Report usage frequency.
4. Include margin comparison.
5. Exportable analytics.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want quotes locked after approval, so that pricing cannot be altered without reopening governance.
Description: Approved quotes must remain immutable.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Lock pricing fields after approval.
2. Require reopen workflow for edits.
3. Log reopen action.
4. Re-trigger approval if modified.
5. Preserve historical snapshot.
